name: Hereditary Hemochromatosis

prevalence.estimate: 1 in 200 to 1 in 500 in Northern European populations

criteria.description: Elevated serum ferritin (>300 ng/mL in men, >200 ng/mL in women)
Hepatic iron concentration >80 µmol/g dry weight on liver biopsy
MRI showing hepatic iron overload (T2* or R2* sequences)
Evidence of iron deposition in target organs

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Elevated transferrin saturation plus either HFE C282Y homozygosity or hepatic iron overload on biopsy/MRI
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Non-HFE hemochromatosis (Types 2-4) involves different genes. Phenotypic expression varies; not all C282Y homozygotes develop clinical disease.

pathognomonic.notes: Generalized slate-gray or bronze discoloration due to iron and melanin deposition

common.notes: 2nd and 3rd MCP joints classically affected; 'iron fist' sign
Due to hypogonadotropic hypogonadism from pituitary iron deposition

occasional.notes: Due to pancreatic iron deposition; part of 'bronze diabetes'
Dilated or restrictive cardiomyopathy from myocardial iron deposition

rare.notes: Risk greatly increased in those with cirrhosis

laboratory: Elevated serum ferritin (often >1000 ng/mL in symptomatic disease)
Low testosterone and gonadotropins in males
imaging: MRI liver with T2*/R2* sequences showing hepatic iron overload
MRI cardiac T2* may show myocardial iron deposition
Radiographs may show chondrocalcinosis in joints
genetic: HFE gene testing: C282Y homozygosity (most common, ~85-90% of cases)
Non-HFE mutations: HJV, HAMP, TFR2, SLC40A1 in non-classical forms
other: Liver biopsy with Perls Prussian blue stain showing parenchymal iron deposition

distinguishingFeatures: History of chronic transfusions or ineffective erythropoiesis
Iron overload secondary to thalassemia, sideroblastic anemia, or MDS
Ferritin may be elevated but transferrin saturation typically <45%
Liver biopsy shows steatosis and Mallory bodies
Mild ferritin elevation but transferrin saturation usually normal
Liver biopsy shows steatosis without significant parenchymal iron
Wilson disease presents with copper overload, not iron
Kayser-Fleischer rings on slit lamp exam

redFlags: Hepatic cirrhosis with risk of hepatocellular carcinoma
Acute heart failure or life-threatening arrhythmias from cardiac iron overload
New-onset diabetes in a patient with liver disease and skin hyperpigmentation
references: Bacon BR, et al. Diagnosis and management of hemochromatosis: 2011 Practice Guideline by AASLD. Hepatology. 2011;54(1):328-343.
European Association for the Study of the Liver. EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines for HFE Hemochromatosis. J Hepatol. 2010;53(1):3-22.
Powell LW, et al. Haemochromatosis. Lancet. 2016;388(10045):706-716.
Barton JC, Edwards CQ. HFE Hemochromatosis. GeneReviews. Updated 2018.
